about: Measured coefficients of restitution (normal, e = -v'n/vn) for flutter3d_matter catalog solids, collected 2026-10-11. Only values read on an opened page/PDF/data file are recorded. 'points' come from three kinds of origin, named in each record: (1) tables in the paper; (2) the digitized e(v) data files that Guttler, Heisselmann, Blum & Krijt published with their survey (arXiv:1204.0001v2 source tarball, files <author>_N.txt), which I log-binned into at most 8 mean points; (3) values I read off a figure myself (stated as 'read off figure', about ±0.01-0.02). a = moving sphere/projectile, b = target, unless the geometry says binary sphere-sphere. Extra pairs outside {self, steel, concrete, wood} are kept when they came with the same source.

pairs.geometry: 12.7 mm steel ball on a pendulum striking a 5 cm thick mild-steel block
pairs.conditions: mirror-polished surfaces; constant ~0.95 below ~0.3 m/s (yield), then falling
pairs.citation: Lifshitz & Kolsky, 'Some experiments on anelastic rebound', J. Mech. Phys. Solids 12 (1964) 35-43, Fig. 1; digitized by Guttler et al., arXiv:1204.0001 (file lifshitz_kolsky.txt)
pairs.note: points are log-bin means of the digitized curve. Before polishing ('finely ground') e never exceeded 0.82; after two polishing steps 0.87 and 0.95 (survey text)

pairs.geometry: 1.29 mm stainless steel ball on a massive stainless steel plate
pairs.citation: Kangur & Kleis, Izv. AN SSSR MTT 5 (1988) 182-185, as presented by Kim & Dunn (2007); digitized by Guttler et al., arXiv:1204.0001 (file kangur_kleis.txt)
pairs.note: high-speed branch; secondhand (Kim & Dunn's replot of a Russian paper)

pairs.impactSpeed: not stated in the chart (binary free-fall apparatus of Foerster et al. 1994: top sphere dropped from 53.9 cm, bottom released from 27.9 cm)

pairs.citation: Louge group (Cornell), 'Fall 1999 Impact Parameter Chart', Impact Results table, row 'Chrome Steel Hoover Precision / Same'
pairs.note: e=1.00±0.01 is at the measurement ceiling; same chart: friction mu=0.12, beta0=0.54

pairs.impactSpeed: 0.64-1.2 m/s (range given by Foerster et al.; constant e is a model assumption over that range)

pairs.citation: Lorenz, Tuozzolo & Louge, Experimental Mechanics 37 (1997) 292-298, Table 1
pairs.note: bead on a similar bead glued to a plate: 0.865±0.011 (0.73-1.67 m/s)

pairs.geometry: binary sphere-sphere, 10 mm smooth soda-lime glass spheres, free fall in a 1.5 m vacuum tube

pairs.citation: Foerster et al., Phys. Fluids 6 (1994) 1108, Table 1 (file foerster_et_al_2.txt in arXiv:1204.0001); Lorenz, Tuozzolo & Louge, Exp. Mech. 37 (1997), Table 1

pairs.geometry: 4.76 mm steel ball bearing on a 1.27 cm thick lucite (PMMA) plate clamped on two sides, impact beyond 2.75 diameters from the support

pairs.note: e depends strongly on sphere diameter / plate thickness (Fig. 3: drops from ~0.9 at a/b->0 to ~0.2 at 2a/2b=1.7), so this is a thin-plate value, not a thick-block one. Open PDF: https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/prznw-f4w71

pairs.citation: King et al., EPL 93 (2011) 14002 (arXiv:cond-mat/0209490), Fig. 4A (squares) and Fig. 3A

pairs.geometry: binary, two 1 m diameter granite spheres (1.3 t) on 15 m crane-suspended cables
pairs.conditions: milled, 'smooth but not polished'; authors give constant 0.8±0.06 (survey text)
pairs.citation: Durda et al., 'Experimental determination of the coefficient of restitution for meter-scale granite spheres', Icarus 211 (2011) 849-855, Fig. 4; digitized by Guttler et al., arXiv:1204.0001 (durda_et_al.txt)
pairs.note: log-bin means of 65 points; no velocity trend

pairs.geometry: 3 mm ball-bearing steel sphere dropped on a polished natural sandstone block
pairs.conditions: e from flight time between bounces (accelerometer on target)
pairs.citation: Imre, Rabsamen & Springman, 'A coefficient of restitution of rock materials', Computers & Geosciences 34 (2008) 339-350; digitized by Guttler et al., arXiv:1204.0001 (imre_et_al.txt)
pairs.note: the paper also tested other targets at one velocity (not in the data file)

pairs.geometry: polycrystalline ice sphere, radius 1.5 cm (as Deckers & Teiser 2016 describe Higa 1996), dropped on a polished decimetre ice block
pairs.citation: Higa, Arakawa & Maeno, 'Measurements of restitution coefficients of ice at low temperatures', Planet. Space Sci. 44 (1996) 917-925, Fig. 5a-c; digitized by Guttler et al., arXiv:1204.0001 (higa_et_al_1..3.txt)
pairs.note: e ~0.9 below a critical speed, then falls as e = eqe (v/vc)^-log(v/vc) (survey's statement of Higa's law); log-bin means

pairs.geometry: 2.5 cm solid ice sphere dropped on a 12 cm ice cylinder
pairs.conditions: 255.8±0.7 K, smooth frost-free; 2 cm sphere: fit e = 0.85 (v/1 m/s)^-1.4; fragmentation thresholds 2.92 m/s (2 cm) and 1.91 m/s (2.5 cm)
pairs.citation: Deckers & Teiser, 'Collisions of solid ice in planetesimal formation', MNRAS (2016), arXiv:1601.04609, Sect. 3.5, Fig. 9 and Eq. 4 (e1 = 0.35, b3 = -0.62 for d = 2.5 cm)
pairs.note: points computed from the paper's published power-law fit, not raw data; measured values scatter 0.1-0.45 in Fig. 9. Hatzes et al. 1988 digitized files in the same survey tarball were skipped because their velocity units look inconsistent with the survey's table (1e-5..1e-2 m/s)

pairs.geometry: near-cubic marble blocks (Penteli marble, two textures) dropped on a 5 cm thick plate of the same marble embedded in plaster on a massive base
pairs.conditions: normal COR read off Fig. 3a: Marble I (SH 38.2) roughly 0.42-0.62; Marble II (SH 50.8) roughly 0.47-0.85; only the 25 % most vertical rebounds kept
pairs.citation: Asteriou, Saroglou & Tsiambaos, 'Correlation between Schmidt hardness and coefficient of restitution of rocks', Bull. Geol. Soc. Greece 47(3) (2013) 1684-1693, Fig. 3a
pairs.note: cubic blocks, not spheres: rotation and corner impacts lower e; ranges read off figure, no single value given

pairs.geometry: near-cubic sparitic limestone blocks (Tourkovounia, Athens) on a 5 cm plate of the same limestone
pairs.conditions: normal COR read off Fig. 3a: roughly 0.37-0.55 (SH 36.1); crystalline limestone (SH 36.7) similar
pairs.citation: Asteriou, Saroglou & Tsiambaos, Bull. Geol. Soc. Greece 47(3) (2013) 1684-1693, Fig. 3a
pairs.note: cubic blocks; ranges read off figure

pairs.geometry: near-cubic quartzitic sandstone blocks (Kalydona tunnel) on a 5 cm plate of the same sandstone
pairs.conditions: normal COR read off Fig. 3a: roughly 0.60-0.76 (SH 44.7)
pairs.citation: Asteriou, Saroglou & Tsiambaos, Bull. Geol. Soc. Greece 47(3) (2013) 1684-1693, Fig. 3a
pairs.note: cubic blocks; ranges read off figure. The same study tested a high-strength cement grout (roughly 0.35-0.62), which is not concrete

pairs.geometry: steel ball bearing (size not given) dropped on a concrete floor
pairs.conditions: e = sqrt(rebound/drop height), mean of 5 drops; same setup: wooden ball 0.603, glass marble 0.658
pairs.citation: Bennett & Meepagala (Midwood High School, 2005), in 'Coefficients of Restitution', The Physics Factbook (ed. G. Elert), 2006
pairs.note: LOW RELIABILITY: high-school measurement, ball sizes and floor build-up unknown; the floor (2nd storey slab) may not act as a massive target. Kept only because no peer-reviewed steel-on-concrete sphere data was found

pairs.geometry: glass marble dropped on a concrete floor
